title: Technical English — Course 3, Semester 2 — Pilot Variant 8

tasks.prompt: Listening 1. When will the terminology workshop take place?
tasks.audioText: The quality department is running a terminology workshop on Tuesday at one thirty in Room 15. Students will review the terms defect, non-conformity, inspection and corrective action. A short glossary will be provided. The instructor asks students to bring one example from a previous classroom exercise where a result did not meet a stated requirement.

tasks.prompt: Listening 2. Which glossary item will be provided?
tasks.audioText: The quality department is running a terminology workshop on Tuesday at one thirty in Room 15. Students will review the terms defect, non-conformity, inspection and corrective action. A short glossary will be provided. The instructor asks students to bring one example from a previous classroom exercise where a result did not meet a stated requirement.

tasks.prompt: A non-conformity is a failure to meet a specified requirement. It may relate to a dimension, material, document or process. A clear report identifies the requirement, describes the observed result and provides relevant evidence. The responsible person can then review the issue and decide what action is appropriate. A non-conformity should not be hidden by changing the original inspection data. Reading 1. What does a non-conformity mean?
options: A failure to meet a specified requirement

tasks.prompt: What should a clear report describe?
options: The requirement, observed result and relevant evidence

tasks.prompt: The original inspection data must not ___ without an authorised correction.
Choose TWO details that help describe a non-conformity.
options: A guess about who is responsible
The requirement that was not met

tasks.prompt: A failure to meet a specified requirement is a non-___.
You need to report a non-conformity. Which sentence is appropriate?
options: The result is wrong, but I will not explain why.
The measured value is outside the specified limit; I have recorded the evidence for review.
I changed the result so it looks correct.

tasks.prompt: Put the stages of quality terminology in a logical order.
options: Compare the result with the requirement
correctOrder: Compare the result with the requirement

tasks.prompt: Write 80–100 words explaining how to report a non-conformity clearly and why original inspection data must remain accurate.
tasks.rubric: 8 points total: the non-conformity is described against a stated requirement with relevant identification/evidence (0–2); the response explains why original inspection data must remain accurate and traceable (0–2); the report is logically organised with understandable grammar (0–2); quality/inspection vocabulary, spelling and punctuation are accurate (0–2).
